text: Invitees can pick a time from a shared booking link, eliminating back-and-forth scheduling emails
quote: Share a booking link, connect your calendars, and let people pick a time without the back-and-forth.

text: Event types can offer multiple selectable durations for the same event
quote: If you want that user can choose between different lengths of the event you can specify them here.

text: Custom fields beyond name/email can be added to the booking form
quote: Custom fields that can be added to the booking form when the event is booked by someone. By default booking form has name and email field.

text: Every booking gets a video location automatically, defaulting to Cal Video or a connected Zoom/Teams/Meet account
quote: Every Cal.com booking gets a location. By default that is Cal Video, and you can point it at Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet instead once the app is connected

text: Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet can be connected at the user or team level
quote: Connect Zoom, Microsoft Teams or Google Meet to a user or a team

text: Bookings (including seated bookings) can be rescheduled, with defined reschedulable statuses like accepted/pending
quote: Reschedule a booking or seated booking. Reschedulable booking statuses: - `accepted` — the confirmed booking is moved to the new start time. - `pending`

text: Available slots for an event type can be queried four different ways (by event type id, by username+slug, by usernames only for dynamic events, etc.)
quote: There are 4 ways to get available slots for event type of an individual user: 1. By event type id. ... 4. By usernames only (used for dynamic event type - there is no specific event but you want to know when 2 or more people are available)

text: Available slots can be queried using just username and event slug, without first looking up IDs
quote: Query available slots using username and event slug—no need to look up IDs first

text: Schedules can be created via API for the authenticated user so event types are available at specific times
quote: Create a schedule for the authenticated user. The point of creating schedules is for event types to be available at specific times.

text: Webhooks can be triggered on booking lifecycle events (created, payment initiated, paid, rescheduled, requested, cancelled)
quote: BOOKING_CREATED - BOOKING_PAYMENT_INITIATED - BOOKING_PAID - BOOKING_RESCHEDULED - BOOKING_REQUESTED - BOOKING_CANCELLED

text: Round-robin events support host priority, weight, group assignment, and advanced settings like no-show calc and CRM fallback
quote: roundRobin: Full configuration including hosts with priority, weight, and group assignment, host groups, and advanced settings (weights toggle, lead threshold, no-show calculations, CRM fallback)

text: Team event types can be flagged as instant meetings via an 'instant' flag in the request body
quote: For team event types it is possible to create instant meeting. To do that just pass "instant": true to the request body.

text: A single bookings endpoint supports creating regular, recurring, and instant bookings
quote: POST /v2/bookings is used to create regular bookings, recurring bookings and instant bookings.

text: A booking's full routing trace (routing forms, CRM lookups, host selection logic) can be retrieved by booking UID
quote: Retrieve the step-by-step routing trace for a booking identified by its UID. Shows how the booking was routed through routing forms, CRM lookups, and host selection logic.

text: Managed users can be created via API that are fully independent of a Cal.com web account, so end users never need to register
quote: a "managed user" is completely independent of a regular user account on cal.com, meaning you don't need your users to register on cal.com web application

text: React 'atoms' let developers embed scheduling UI directly into their own product
quote: Find out how to use Cal "atoms" to integrate scheduling into your product.

text: A hosted MCP server at mcp.cal.com (or a self-run instance) lets AI clients connect to Cal.com scheduling
quote: Connect AI clients to Cal.com scheduling through the Model Context Protocol using the hosted server at mcp.cal.com or a local instance.

text: API v2 lets AI agents check availability, create bookings, and manage event types on users' behalf
quote: Cal.com API v2 enables AI agents to: Check availability - Query available time slots for any user or team, Create bookings - Schedule meetings on behalf of users

text: API supports three authentication methods: OAuth, API key, and (deprecated) platform auth
quote: The Cal.com API has 3 authentication methods: 1. OAuth 2. API key 3. Platform (Deprecated)

text: API keys can be created and managed from the account security settings page
quote: You can view and manage your API keys in your settings page under the security tab in Cal.com.

text: Cal.diy is a 100% MIT-licensed fork of Cal.com with all enterprise/commercial code removed, for self-hosters
quote: Cal.diy is 100% MIT-licensed with no proprietary "Enterprise Edition" features. It's designed for individuals and self-hosters who want full control over their scheduling infrastructure

text: Product powers one-on-one, group, round-robin and collective scheduling with routing forms, workflows, payments, native video, and an app store
quote: It powers one-on-one, group, round-robin, and collective scheduling, with routing forms, workflows, payments, native video, and an app store of integrations.

text: OAuth clients can be created to let users 'Continue with Cal.com' for third-party integrations
quote: Create an OAuth client and "Continue with Cal.com"

text: API authentication is performed via a standard Authorization header
quote: Authentication to the API is performed via the Authorization header.

text: MCP integration lets users manage bookings, event types and schedules through natural language in any MCP-compatible client
quote: letting you manage bookings, event types, schedules, and more through natural language in any MCP-compatible client

text: Event types can be created programmatically via the API
quote: Create an event type

text: The scheduling configuration for a team event type can be retrieved via API
quote: Returns the scheduling configuration for a team event type.

text: Product supports HIPAA (with BAA), SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA compliance
quote: Compliance is a core differentiator. Cal.com supports HIPAA (with BAA available on organization/enterprise plans), SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR, and CCPA.

text: Key differentiators include a self-hostable MIT edition, API-first architecture, regulated-industry compliance, org-scale governance and a generous free tier
quote: For evaluators comparing against Calendly: Cal.com's differentiators are the self-hostable MIT edition (Cal.diy), API-first architecture, regulated-industry compliance, organization-scale governance, and a generous free tier.

text: An official Cal.com CLI is recommended for agents that can execute commands on a machine, instead of calling the API directly
quote: For agents that can execute commands on a machine, use the official Cal.com CLI instead of calling the API directly.

text: The booking creation endpoint is public and requires no authentication, allowing agents to book on behalf of external users
quote: The booking creation endpoint is public and does not require authentication. This allows agents to book on behalf of external users.

text: Slot/availability lookups accept eventTypeSlug and username (plus optional organizationSlug for org members) as parameters
quote: Provide `eventTypeSlug` and `username` and optionally `organizationSlug` if the user with the username is within an organization.
